learning_extracted: A genuine, well-powered, mechanistically-interpretable dissociation: abort mechanism works exactly as designed informationally (C2 passes) but this does not translate to lower harm (C1 fails) -- structurally guaranteed by the current implementation, not ambiguous.

REE's fear/threat proto-emotion machinery (BLA/CeA, MECH-357/SD-058) exists and biases action choice elsewhere (E3 scoring, the separate MECH-091 urgency-interrupt abort) but is not connected to MECH-321's redecomposition. MECH-288 (MECH-321's own trigger) is purely predictive-surprise-based.

The hippocampal motivational payload (SD-039 AnchorGoalPayload) is architecturally the more natural coupling point than the raw amygdala signal, but currently carries only reward-valence, not harm-valence, and is not wired into _apply_policy_decomposition regardless.
This is a well-localized, buildable substrate gap once specified: no existing substrate_queue entry or claim covers hazard-aware policy-decomposition retiling (verified).

investigation_note.trigger: User mid-autopsy question: does REE's fear/proto-emotion machinery bias mid-execution redecomposition toward defensive/lower-harm paths, and if so is that why C1 fails while C2 passes?
investigation_note.method: Two rounds of code-grounded investigation (Explore agent) against ree_core/ and claims.yaml, not speculation.
investigation_note.outcome: Coherent hypothesis, retargeted: MECH-288 (MECH-321's trigger) is threat-unrelated; the real fear pathway (MECH-091) is a separate, parallel abort mechanism; the redecomposition step itself has no harm-valence input and no selection mechanism of any kind. This directly explains the C1/C2 dissociation and produced a new, specific, actionable recommended_substrate_queue_entry not previously in claims.yaml or substrate_queue.json.
